cells.tense: The decision is being made in this moment, and your hands are on it.
cells.ask: Pick one direction you've been circling and say it out loud to someone today, in plain words, no pitch.
cells.core:
When a direction lights up, you say yes and start moving before you can see the whole road. The clarity arrives after the step, not before it. What you're carrying is a yes that hasn't been tested against the world yet — and that's the workable part, because it moves.

The balance is in not waiting for the full picture before you commit. Say one direction to one person today, plainly, and take one step another person could watch you take. The confidence doesn't need guarding and it doesn't need proof. It gets cleaner each time you move on it without checking first.
cells.sheetLine: You point yourself somewhere and start moving before you can see it all.
cells.verb: lighting up with a direction before you know where it goes
cells.place: the part of you that chooses which way to go

cells.tense: You're bracing for how it will land before the thing has even left your hands.
cells.ask: Say the direction once to one person and leave the room before you explain it — let their face finish before you add anything.
cells.core:
The fire is running ahead of the thing it's for. Before a direction is even yours, it's already performing — how it'll sound, what it'll prove, who it'll move. The pulse is real. But you're spending it on a reaction that hasn't happened, and the version you're pitching keeps outrunning the one you actually had.

Shine that comes from something grown is steadier than shine that's timed. Say one direction to one person and let them answer before you add anything to it. Letting the sentence land before you fix it is the whole practice. The answer can be anything. What matters is that you let it come.

cells.tense: A door you walked through a while back is still standing in front of you tonight.
cells.ask: Tell one friend a direction you're drawn to, badly, without a plan, and let it stay unfinished when you stop talking.
cells.core:
A direction lights up and it moves — that's the version where this is working. You say it, someone hears it, and the yes turns into something a person could watch you do. Right now the pull is there and it isn't moving. The saying stopped, and the not-saying held. The fire hasn't gone out. You stopped pointing at anything.

Don't try to force the confidence back. Attention works better than effort here. Tell one person, badly, a direction you're drawn to. Aliveness comes back through caring for a small thing, not through deciding to be radiant. Give a little care to something and see what comes back with it. You don't need to know where it goes. Start anyway.

cells.tense: You're steering something already, and you're talking about it as if it just showed up.
cells.ask: Name one thing you set in motion this month and say, to someone, 'I chose that,' before adding what happened next.
cells.core:
You're already pointing people somewhere — the energy, the direction, the way a room moves when you're behind something. When it's working well, that energy is steady and visible; you commit, and the commitment shows in what happens next. Right now you describe it as though it happened on its own. 'It just came up.' 'One thing led to another.' The steering is real. The saying-so isn't.

Capability that holds contains instead of pushes. Say 'I chose that' about one thing you set in motion this month, once, and don't soften it with what followed. You've been at the wheel the whole time. The missing piece is only you saying so.
cells.sheetLine: 'It just happened' isn't true. You turned the wheel.
